text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a pruritic rash on your bilateral upper extremities; to help identify the cause, please describe when the rash first appeared and if it changes with heat or sweating. Did you notice any new soaps, detergents, or jewelry on those arms recently?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The images show symmetric, erythematous, scaly plaques affecting the extensor surfaces of the elbows and knuckles. Have you recently noticed your skin tightening or becoming difficult to stretch over your knuckles? Also, do you have any joint pain or swelling in your hands or fingers?

REQUEST TEST: Rheumatoid_Factor, Anti-CCP, ANA.
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_Close_Up_Knuckles_Elbows.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Dermatomyositis. The clinical presentation of a pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities (specifically symmetric, scaly plaques on the knuckles and elbows) combined with your query about skin tightening and joint pain is highly suggestive of this condition, which is an inflammatory myopathy characterized by pathognomonic skin rashes. While we have not yet received specific confirmation of muscle weakness or elevated muscle enzymes, the cutaneous findings on the extensor surfaces are the primary diagnostic clue. Please continue to monitor for proximal muscle weakness (difficulty raising your arms or standing from a chair). If these symptoms develop, we will immediately proceed with requesting Creatine Kinase (CK), Aldolase, and an electromyogram (EMG).
